source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. X (Montreuil)

1.title: Expositio litteralis capituli primi: Verba Amos, qui fuit in pastoralibus Thecue.
1.title_en: Literal exposition of the first chapter: The words of Amos, who was among the herdsmen of Thecua.

paras.t: Præmittit autem Amos nunc elucidandus prologum sive proœmium, dicens: Verba Amos, qui fuit in pastoralibus Thecue, id est in locis prædictæ solitudinis aptis ad greges pascendos. Pastoralia itaque dicit loca vicina urbi Thecue, in quibus nascuntur non segetes, sed pascua gregum. Quæ verba vidit, id est, intellectualiter Deo illustrante cognovit: a qua visione Prophetæ dicebantur Videntes. Intelligentia enim est opus in visione. Et certum est, quod verba proprie non videntur visu exteriori atque carnali. Super Israel, id est decem tribus, quia pro majori parte et principaliter verba ista ad decem tribus pertinebant: non tamen omnia pertinebant ad eas, sicut patebit. In diebus Oziæ regis Juda, et in diebus Jeroboam filii Joas regis Israel. Iste est Ozias, alio nomine Azarias, pater Joathan patris Achaz: qui Ozias regnavit in Jerusalem quinquaginta duobus annis. Jeroboam vero iste, est filius Joas filii Joachaz, filii Jehu, cui spoponderat Dominus quod filii ejus usque ad quartam generationem sederent in throno Israel. Hæc autem plenius dicta sunt in expositione primi capituli Osee.
paras.en: Amos, who is now to be explained, first sets down a prologue or proem, saying: [[1:1|The words of Amos, who was among the herdsmen of Thecua|Verba Amos, qui fuit in pastoralibus Thecue]] [Denis reads *in pastoralibus*, "in the pasture-lands", where the Vulgate has *in pastoribus*, "among the herdsmen"], that is, in the places of the aforesaid wilderness that are suited to pasturing flocks. So by pasture-lands he means the places near the town of Thecua in which no crops grow, but pasture for flocks. [[1:1|which he saw|Quæ verba vidit]], that is, which he knew intellectually by God's enlightening: from which seeing the Prophets were called Seers[[1 Kings 9:9||]]. Indeed, [[Dan 10:1|there is need of understanding in a vision|Intelligentia enim est opus in visione]]. And it is certain that words, properly speaking, are not seen by the outward and bodily sight. [[1:1|concerning Israel|Super Israel]], that is, the ten tribes, because for the most part and chiefly these words concerned the ten tribes; yet not all of them concerned them, as will appear. [[1:1|in the days of Ozias king of Juda, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joas king of Israel|In diebus Oziæ regis Juda, et in diebus Jeroboam filii Joas regis Israel]]. This is Ozias, by another name Azarias[[4 Kings 15:1||]][[2 Par 26:1||]], the father of Joatham the father of Achaz; this Ozias reigned in Jerusalem two and fifty years[[4 Kings 15:2||]]. And this Jeroboam is the son of Joas[[4 Kings 13:13||]], the son of Joachaz[[4 Kings 13:10||]], the son of Jehu, to whom the Lord had promised that his sons would sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation[[4 Kings 10:30||]]. But these things were said more fully in the exposition of the first chapter of Osee[[Osee 1:4||]].

paras.t: Vidit autem Amos verba infra ponenda, ante duos annos terræ motus, id est ante duos annos antequam Ozias rex thurificare præsumpsit in templo. Ad cujus culpam increpandam, ostendendam, ac puniendam, ipse Ozias non solum percussus est lepra, sed etiam terræ motus factus fuit in templo. De quo terræ motu in libris Regum et Paralipomenon reticetur, sed hoc loco et in Zacharia fit mentio inde. Dicit enim Zacharias: Fugietis, sicut fugistis a facie terræ motus in diebus Oziæ regis. Interdum autem dicitur Ozias usurpasse officium sacerdotale in thurificando ex animi elatione, interdum vero ex nimio religionis affectu et zelo cultus divini. Unde in prologo ait Glossa: Ozias rex quum Dei religionem sollicite æmularetur, nimio religionis amore provocatus, contra legis præceptum, sacerdotale officium præsumere est conatus. Verum hæc duo stant simul. In hoc enim fuit superbia, quod nec post exhortationem pontificis et commemorationem divinæ jussionis, quam proposuit pontifex regi Oziæ, cessavit a proposito cordis: et forte propter regiam celsitudinem putavit se dignum ad thurificandum. In hoc autem fuit amor quidam religionis et zelus Dei, quod hoc ipsum agere attentaverit, tanquam opus venerationis divinæ, et ad augendum seu magnificandum cultum divinum. Unde de incredulis Judæis dixit Apostolus, quod æmulationem Dei habent, sed non secundum scientiam. Sic quoque et Gedeon zelo quodam Dei, sed indiscreto, fecit sibi ephod sacerdotale, quod factum est sibi et domui suæ in ruinam, ut scriptum est in libro Judicum.
paras.en: Now Amos saw the words set down below [[1:1|two years before the earthquake|ante duos annos terræ motus]], that is, two years before King Ozias presumed to burn incense in the temple[[2 Par 26:16||]]. To rebuke, to show forth and to punish his fault, not only was Ozias himself struck with leprosy[[2 Par 26:19||]], but there was also an earthquake in the temple. Of this earthquake the books of Kings and of Paralipomenon say nothing, but it is mentioned here and in Zacharias. For Zacharias says: [[Zach 14:5|you shall flee as you fled from the face of the earthquake in the days of Ozias king|Fugietis, sicut fugistis a facie terræ motus in diebus Oziæ regis]]. Now sometimes Ozias is said to have usurped the priestly office in burning incense out of pride of mind, and sometimes out of an excessive devotion to religion and zeal for the worship of God. Hence the Gloss says in the prologue: King Ozias, since he was earnestly zealous for the religion of God, provoked by an excessive love of religion, attempted against the precept of the law to presume upon the priestly office. But these two stand together. For there was pride in this, that not even after the exhortation of the high priest and his reminder of the divine command, which the high priest put before King Ozias[[2 Par 26:18||]][[2 Par 26:19||]], did he desist from the purpose of his heart; and perhaps on account of his royal eminence he thought himself worthy to burn incense. But there was a certain love of religion and zeal for God in this, that he attempted to do this very thing as a work of divine worship, and to increase or magnify the worship of God. Hence the Apostle said of the unbelieving Jews that [[Rom 10:2|they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge|æmulationem Dei habent, sed non secundum scientiam]]. So too Gedeon, out of a certain zeal for God, but an indiscreet one, made himself a priestly ephod, which turned to the ruin of himself and of his house[[Judg 8:27||]], as is written in the book of Judges.

paras.t: Consequenter ponitur narratio seu tractatus. Et dixit Amos ad populum decem tribuum. Ut enim annuntiaret hæc verba populo, revelata sunt ei. Dominus de Sion rugiet, et de Jerusalem dabit vocem suam. Hæc verba in propria forma scripta sunt apud Joelem, atque in præcedentibus exposita. Verumtamen alium sensum, etiam quantum ad litteram, habent ibi, et alium hic. Siquidem ibi dicta sunt pro die finalis judicii, in quo Christus tanquam leo horrendam sententiam proferet contra perversos, a loco in quo residebit, videlicet in aere circa montem Oliveti, et prope Jerusalem. Nunc autem dicuntur de captivitate decem tribuum Israel, ut sit sensus: Dominus de Sion, id est Deus omnipotens, qui commoratur in templo suo sito in monte Sion, rugiet de hoc habitationis suæ loco. Dominus enim in templo suo sancto, terribiliter quasi leo loquetur contra decem tribus. Et de Jerusalem civitate sancta, in qua fuit cultus ejus, et populus fidelis, in quo habitavit per gratiam, dabit vocem suam, id est propheticam prænuntiationem seu comminationem de decem tribuum captivitate ab Assyriis facta.
paras.en: Next comes the narrative or treatise. [[1:2|And he said|Et dixit]], that is, Amos, to the people of the ten tribes; for these words were revealed to him so that he might announce them to the people. [[1:2|The Lord will roar from Sion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem|Dominus de Sion rugiet, et de Jerusalem dabit vocem suam]]. These words are written in exactly the same form in Joel[[Joel 3:16||]], and have been explained in what went before. Yet they have one sense there, even as to the letter, and another here. For there they are said of the day of the last judgment, in which Christ, as a lion, will pronounce the dreadful sentence against the wicked[[Matt 25:41||]] from the place where he will be seated, namely in the air about Mount Olivet, near Jerusalem. But here they are said of the captivity of the ten tribes of Israel, so that the sense is: [[1:2|The Lord|Dominus]] [[1:2|from Sion|de Sion]], that is, God almighty, who abides in his temple set on Mount Sion, [[1:2|will roar|rugiet]] from this place of his dwelling. For [[Ps 10:5|The Lord is in his holy temple|Dominus enim in templo suo sancto]], and will speak terribly, as a lion, against the ten tribes. And [[1:2|from Jerusalem|de Jerusalem]], the holy city, in which was his worship, and the faithful people in whom he dwelt by grace, he will [[1:2|utter his voice|dabit vocem suam]], that is, the prophetic foretelling or threat of the captivity of the ten tribes brought about by the Assyrians.

paras.t: Hæc autem dicuntur, vel quia per Prophetas qui erant in Jerusalem, Deus prædixit hanc captivitatem; vel quia Deus, qui ubique est, dicitur specialiter de Sion loqui, quemadmodum ibi specialiter se esse et habitare asseruit (unde in libro Regum frequenter legitur, quod Jerusalem elegit, ut poneret nomen suum in ea, et quod templum sibi sanctificavit, ut habitaret in eo); vel quia, ut aliqui dicunt, in visione imaginaria ipsi Amos ostensa, videbatur sibi quod vox Dei ad ipsum de illo loco procederet, quemadmodum Jacob patriarchæ in Bethel apparuit in visione imaginaria quod Deus loqueretur ad ipsum ab arce scalæ, cui videbatur innixus. Idcirco Propheta non dicit: Dominus de Bethel, vel Dan, vel de Samaria rugiet: quia in illis locis idololatriæ deditis non habitavit, quum Salomon in Proverbiis dicat, Longe est Dominus ab impiis.
paras.en: Now these things are said either because God foretold this captivity through the Prophets who were in Jerusalem; or because God, who is everywhere, is said to speak especially from Sion, as he declared that he especially is and dwells there[[Ps 83:2||]][[Ps 75:3||]][[Ps 98:2||]] (hence we often read in the book of Kings that he chose Jerusalem to put his name there[[3 Kings 11:36||]][[2 Par 7:16||]], and that he sanctified the temple to himself to dwell in it[[3 Kings 9:3||]][[2 Par 6:2||]]); or because, as some say, in an imaginary vision [that is, a vision of images formed in the imagination, as distinct from a bodily or a purely intellectual one] shown to Amos himself, it seemed to him that the voice of God came to him from that place, as it appeared to the patriarch Jacob at Bethel, in an imaginary vision, that God spoke to him from the top of the ladder on which he seemed to lean[[Gen 28:12||]][[Gen 28:13||]]. Therefore the Prophet does not say: The Lord will roar from Bethel, or Dan, or from Samaria; for he did not dwell in those places given over to idolatry, since Solomon says in the Proverbs, [[Prov 15:29|The Lord is far from the wicked|Longe est Dominus ab impiis]].

paras.t: Porro, ut ait Glossa, et sumptum est ex commento Hieronymi: Naturale est ut omnes qui volunt rem unam alteri comparare, ex his rebus sumant comparationem quas sunt experti, et in quibus sunt nutriti: quemadmodum nauta adversarios suos comparat vento, damnum naufragio, tristitiam tempestati, prosperitatem seu jucunditatem placidæ auræ. Sic quoque in ore philosophorum semper versantur Socrates, Plato, Aristoteles, Xenophon, Zenon, Theophrastus. Sic Amos pastor in eremo vasta feris plena, iram seu comminationem Dei, rugitui leonis assimilat. Erat autem rusticanus. Unde et infra simili artis suæ utens exemplo, disseruit: Dominus stridebit super vos, sicut stridet plaustrum onustum fœno.
paras.en: Moreover, as the Gloss says (and it is taken from Jerome's commentary): It is natural that all who wish to compare one thing with another should take the comparison from the things they have experienced and among which they were brought up: as a sailor compares his enemies to the wind, a loss to a shipwreck, sorrow to a storm, prosperity or gladness to a gentle breeze. So too Socrates, Plato, Aristotle, Xenophon, Zeno, Theophrastus are always on the lips of philosophers. So Amos, a herdsman in a vast wilderness full of wild beasts, likens the wrath or threat of God to the roaring of a lion. For he was a countryman. Hence below also, using a like example from his own craft, he said: The Lord will screak over you, [[Amos 2:13|as a wain screaketh that is laden with hay|sicut stridet plaustrum onustum fœno]] [the Vulgate begins "Behold, I will screak under you"].

paras.t: Et luxerunt speciosa pastorum: id est, comminatione Dei præfata impleta, plana loca camporum, viridia loca pratorum, agri herbis fructibusque ornati, in quibus pastores pecora aluerunt, desolata sunt atque vastata, quando videlicet hostes prædicti terram decem tribuum destruxerunt. Quemadmodum enim loca ista metaphorice ridere dicuntur, dum speciosis fructibus seu floribus adornantur, sic lugent, quando his privata, in sterilitatem quamdam seu ariditatem rediguntur. Et exsiccatus est vertex Carmeli. Duo sunt montes, qui apud Græcos atque Latinos Carmeli, apud Hebræos autem Chermel, vocantur. Unus, in quo habitavit Nabal maritus Abigail; alter, in quo oravit, pluviamque impetravit Elias. Vertices itaque, id est superiora horum montium loca, per sterilitatem exsiccata sunt vel vastata. Vel per speciosa pastorum intelliguntur potentes ac divites, vel, secundum aliquos, universi habitatores regni decem tribuum; per verticem vero Carmeli, rex Israel, puta Osee ultimus rex Israel ab Assyriis interfectus: tuncque omnis populus ejus luxit.
paras.en: [[1:2|and the beautiful places of the shepherds have mourned|Et luxerunt speciosa pastorum]]: that is, when the aforesaid threat of God was fulfilled, the level places of the plains, the green places of the meadows, the fields adorned with grass and fruits, in which the shepherds fed their flocks, were made desolate and laid waste, namely when the enemies spoken of destroyed the land of the ten tribes. For as such places are said metaphorically to laugh when they are adorned with beautiful fruits or flowers, so they mourn when, deprived of these, they are brought to a kind of barrenness or dryness. [[1:2|and the top of Carmel is withered|Et exsiccatus est vertex Carmeli]]. There are two mountains which among the Greeks and Latins are called Carmel, but among the Hebrews Chermel. On the one dwelt Nabal the husband of Abigail[[1 Kings 25:2||]][[1 Kings 25:3||]]; on the other Elias prayed and obtained rain[[3 Kings 18:42||]]. So the tops, that is, the upper parts of these mountains, were withered or laid waste by barrenness. Or by the beautiful places of the shepherds are meant the mighty and the rich, or, according to some, all the inhabitants of the kingdom of the ten tribes; and by the top of Carmel the king of Israel, namely Osee, the last king of Israel, slain by the Assyrians: and then all his people mourned.

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus: Super tribus sceleribus Damasci, et super quatuor non convertam eum. Verba ista intricata sunt valde, et quantum ex commentis quæ vidi colligere possum, iste est sensus: Super tribus sceleribus, id est de tribus peccatis Damasci, id est regni Syriæ, quæ per Damascum notatur, quia Damascus erat metropolis Syriæ, juxta illud Isaiæ, Caput Syriæ Damascus; et super quatuor, id est de prædictis peccatis quarto reiteratis, non convertam eum, id est, ei non parcam, dando pœnitentiæ gratiam, vel a debitis punitionibus liberationem. Tanquam dicat, secundum Hieronymum: Si semel esset populum meum Israel persecutus, aut secundo, darem veniam; nunc vero, quoniam tertio et quarto crudelis fuit in eum, non parcam. Quod Glossa apertius exprimit, dicens in speciali: Si Hazael rex Syriæ et populus ejus semel et bis tantummodo populum meum esset persecutus, forsitan parcerem eis. Sed quia diu exspectavi eorum pœnitentiam, et ipsi econtra mea longanimitate abusi, tertio et quarto populum Israel afflixerunt, plagis corripiam delinquentes. — Ex quo apparet, quod iste sit sensus: Si tribus vicibus tantum, videlicet semel et bis, prædictum malum fecissent, remissibile esset; sed quoniam tertio et quarto hoc fecerunt, id est, peccato ter iterato quartum simile adjecerunt, quatuor vicibus tribulando Israelem, non ignoscam. Huic sensui concordat illud in prologo: Quoniam Amos propheta ait, Super tribus sceleribus, et super quatuor non transferam eum, tertio peccatorum indulgentiam Deum dare posse significat, quem quarto eadem peccata facientibus, nec pœnitentiam, nec indulgentiam daturum enuntiat. Hoc idem insinuat Glossa in morali horum verborum expositione, prout in sequenti articulo patebit. Unde et Lyra hoc loco refert esse opinionem Hebræorum, quod si peccaverit homo bis vel ter eodem genere peccati, sit remissibile; non autem, si quater. Ad quod allegari posset illud in libro Job: Ecce hæc operatur Deus tribus vicibus per singulos.
paras.en: [[1:3|Thus saith the Lord: For three crimes of Damascus, and for four I will not convert it|Hæc dicit Dominus: Super tribus sceleribus Damasci, et super quatuor non convertam eum]]. These words are very intricate, and as far as I can gather from the commentaries I have seen, this is the sense: [[1:3|For three crimes|Super tribus sceleribus]], that is, for three sins of Damascus, that is, of the kingdom of Syria, which is signified by Damascus because Damascus was the capital of Syria, according to that of Isaias: [[Is 7:8|the head of Syria is Damascus|Caput Syriæ Damascus]]; [[1:3|and for four|et super quatuor]], that is, for the said sins repeated a fourth time, [[1:3|I will not convert it|non convertam eum]], that is, I will not spare it by giving it the grace of penance, or deliverance from the punishments it deserves. As if he were saying, according to Jerome: If it had persecuted my people Israel once, or a second time, I would grant pardon; but now, since it has been cruel to them a third and a fourth time, I will not spare. This the Gloss expresses more plainly, saying in particular: If Azael king of Syria and his people had persecuted my people only once and twice, perhaps I would have spared them. But because I long awaited their penance, and they on the contrary, abusing my long-suffering, afflicted the people of Israel a third and a fourth time, I will chastise the offenders with stripes. From this it appears that this is the sense: If they had done the said evil three times only, namely once and twice, it would be pardonable; but since they did it a third and a fourth time, that is, to a sin thrice repeated they added a fourth like it, troubling Israel four times, I will not forgive. With this sense agrees what is said in the prologue: Since the prophet Amos says, [[1:3|For three crimes|Super tribus sceleribus]], [[1:3|and for four|et super quatuor]] I will not transfer it [*non transferam eum*; the margin gives the Vulgate's *convertam*, "I will not convert it"], he signifies that the third time God can grant pardon of sins, but declares that to those who commit the same sins a fourth time he will give neither penance nor pardon. The Gloss suggests the same in its moral exposition of these words, as will appear in the following article. Hence Lyra too reports here that it is the opinion of the Hebrews that if a man has sinned twice or three times in the same kind of sin, it is pardonable; but not if four times. In support of which could be alleged that passage in the book of Job: [[Job 33:29|Behold, all these things God worketh three times within every one|Ecce hæc operatur Deus tribus vicibus per singulos]].

paras.t: Sed quomodo intelligenda sunt hæc, quum Dominus per Ezechielem dicat, Quia quacumque hora peccator ingemiscit, omnium iniquitatum ejus non recordabor? Constat quoque quod Jephthe et Manasses inter electos sint, quorum alter latrociniis, alter idololatriis, diu ac frequentissime deservivit. Nabuchodonosor insuper regem, post varia crimina sæpissime repetita, Daniel ad pœnitentiam provocavit. Et sicut Salomon ait in Ecclesiaste, In quocumque loco ceciderit lignum, ibi erit. Ex quo constat, quemlibet posse misericordiam consequi durante vita præsenti, ita quod in morte dumtaxat est terminus meritorum. — Prædicta denique videntur propinquare hæresi Novatianorum, pœnitentiam lapsis negantium.
paras.en: But how are these things to be understood, since the Lord says through Ezechiel: At whatever hour the sinner groans[[Ezech 18:21||]], [[Ezech 18:22|I will not remember all his iniquities|omnium iniquitatum ejus non recordabor]]? [the first words are the form in which this saying was commonly quoted; Ezechiel's own words are "if the wicked do penance for all his sins"] It is certain too that Jephte[[Heb 11:32||]] and Manasses[[2 Par 33:12||]] are among the elect, of whom the one gave himself long and very often to robbery[[Judg 11:3||]], the other to idolatry[[4 Kings 21:2||]]. Moreover Daniel called King Nabuchodonosor to penance after various crimes very often repeated[[Dan 4:24||]]. And, as Solomon says in Ecclesiastes, [[Eccles 11:3|in what place soever it shall fall, there shall it be|In quocumque loco ceciderit lignum, ibi erit]]. From which it is clear that anyone can obtain mercy while the present life lasts, so that only at death is the term of merits. Lastly, what has been said seems to come near the heresy of the Novatians [the followers of Novatian, a third-century Roman schismatic], who denied penance to the lapsed.

paras.t: Et respondendum, quod Deus interdum punit peccata sine dilatione, antequam iterentur; interdum exspectat vel magis vel minus, secundum incomprehensibilem suæ voluntatis libertatem ac æquitatem, vel etiam pietatem. In Syris autem et ceteris gentibus quæ sequuntur, placuit sibi in quarto peccato ulcisci. Peccatum autem irremissibile dicitur dupliciter: primo, quia nequaquam dimittitur, ut est finalis impœnitentia; secundo, quoniam difficulter ignoscitur, quemadmodum ait Salvator: Qui blasphemaverit in Spiritum Sanctum, non habebit remissionem in æternum. Hæc autem difficultas, est ex parte peccati, ratione suæ enormitatis; vel peccantis, quia sæpe eadem vitia repetendo, divina miseratione se indignum constituit: non autem ex parte Dei, cujus potentia atque clementia prorsus infinita consistit. Sic ergo nunc loquitur Dominus. Quod si Hebræi vellent asserere, quod idem genus peccati, quarto reiteratum ab eodem, nullo modo sit remissibile, errarent, sicut in multis aliis errant.
paras.en: The answer must be that God sometimes punishes sins without delay, before they are repeated; sometimes he waits a longer or a shorter time, according to the incomprehensible freedom and equity, or even the loving-kindness, of his will. In the case of the Syrians and of the other nations that follow, it pleased him to take vengeance at the fourth sin. Now a sin is called unpardonable in two ways: first, because it is never forgiven, as is final impenitence; secondly, because it is pardoned with difficulty, as the Saviour says: [[Mark 3:29|he that shall blaspheme against the Holy Ghost, shall never have forgiveness|Qui blasphemaverit in Spiritum Sanctum, non habebit remissionem in æternum]]. This difficulty, however, is on the part of the sin, by reason of its enormity; or of the sinner, because by often repeating the same vices he makes himself unworthy of the divine mercy: but not on the part of God, whose power and clemency are altogether infinite. So, then, the Lord speaks here. But if the Hebrews wished to assert that the same kind of sin, repeated a fourth time by the same person, is in no way pardonable, they would err, as they err in many other things.

paras.t: Præterea, causa punitionis Syriæ subditur. Eo quod trituraverit, id est, contriverit atque occiderit, in plaustris ferreis, id est per instrumenta quædam ferreos dentes habentia, Galaad, id est populum Israel habitantem trans Jordanem, in regione vel civitate nomine Galaad, quæ cessit mediæ tribui Manasse. Galaad autem est nomen regionis illius, et etiam civitatis. Recteque dicitur, Trituraverit. Quemadmodum enim prædictis instrumentis, seu rotis subter ferratis atque dentatis, excutiuntur in Palæstina frumenta in horreis, sic ut et stipula quasi in paleam redigatur, deturque jumentis in escam propter fœni defectum; sic Hazael et Syri per instrumenta hujusmodi crudeliter contriverunt Galaaditas, juxta illud quarti libri Regum: Non sunt derelicti Joachaz regi Israel de populo suo, nisi quinquaginta equites, et decem currus, et decem millia peditum: interfecerat enim eos rex Syriæ, et redegerat quasi pulverem in tritura areæ.
paras.en: Further, the cause of Syria's punishment is added: [[1:3|because they have thrashed|Eo quod trituraverit]], that is, crushed and slain, [[1:3|with iron wains|in plaustris ferreis]], that is, with certain instruments having iron teeth, [[1:3|Galaad|Galaad]], that is, the people of Israel dwelling beyond the Jordan, in the region or city named Galaad, which fell to the half tribe of Manasses[[Jos 17:1||]][[Jos 17:6||]]. Galaad is the name of that region, and also of a city. And rightly is it said, *thrashed*. For as with the said instruments, or wheels shod with iron and toothed underneath, the corn is threshed out in Palestine in the barns, so that the straw too is reduced as it were to chaff and given to the beasts for fodder for want of hay; so Azael and the Syrians cruelly crushed the Galaadites with instruments of this kind, according to that of the fourth book of Kings: [[4 Kings 13:7|Joachaz had no more left of the people than fifty horsemen, and ten chariots, and ten thousand footmen: for the king of Syria had slain them, and had brought them low as dust by threshing in the barnfloor|Non sunt derelicti Joachaz regi Israel de populo suo, nisi quinquaginta equites, et decem currus, et decem millia peditum: interfecerat enim eos rex Syriæ, et redegerat quasi pulverem in tritura areæ]].

paras.t: Quæritur, cur comminatio Dei primo contra Damascum dirigitur. Ad hoc multi respondent, quod ideo quoniam tempore quo Amos prophetavit, Hazael graviter urgebat decem tribus. Sed objici potest, quod Amos prophetavit sub Jeroboam et Ozia, ante quos Hazael diu mortuus fuit: quia ut quarto Regum describitur, Joas rex Israel pater prædicti Jeroboam, pugnavit contra Benadad filium Hazaelis, tribusque vicibus superavit eum, quemadmodum Eliseus moriens prænuntiavit, quando videlicet præcepit Joas regi ut jaculo percuteret terram. Et palam est, quod Hazael tunc mortuus fuit. Jeroboam vero præfatus successit Joas patri suo in regnum. Potest ergo aliter dici, videlicet quod tempore Amos adhuc persecutio Hazaelis et filii ejus erat magis in recordatione, quia non diu præcessit, quam persecutiones aliorum in filios Israel, quæ infra ponentur, et forte factæ fuerunt vivente ipso Amos, quamvis nondum prophetante. Patet quoque ex dictis, quod plaustra non sumuntur hoc loco pro curribus: propter quod Septuaginta pro plaustris posuerunt ferreas serras.
paras.en: It is asked why God's threat is directed first against Damascus. To this many answer that it is because at the time when Amos prophesied, Azael was pressing hard upon the ten tribes. But it can be objected that Amos prophesied under Jeroboam and Ozias, before whose time Azael had long been dead: for, as is described in the fourth book of Kings, Joas king of Israel, the father of the aforesaid Jeroboam, fought against Benadad the son of Azael and overcame him three times, as Eliseus foretold when he was dying, namely when he commanded King Joas to strike the ground with a javelin. And it is plain that Azael was then dead; and the aforesaid Jeroboam succeeded his father Joas in the kingdom. It can therefore be said otherwise: namely that in the time of Amos the persecution by Azael and his son was still more in memory, because it had gone before not long since, than the persecutions of the children of Israel by the others, which are set down below, and which perhaps took place in the lifetime of Amos himself, though before he was prophesying. It is clear also from what has been said that *wains* are not taken here for war-chariots: for which reason the Septuagint put iron saws in place of wains.

paras.t: Deinde subjungitur Syrorum punitio. Et mittam ignem, id est gravem punitionem, irrevocabilem iram, seu captivitatem, in domum Hazael, id est in ejus progeniem; et devorabit domos Benadad, id est posteros vel etiam habitacula filii Hazaelis, qui dictus est Benadad. Dicit autem Glossa, quod pater Hazaelis vocatus est Benadab, habens ultimam litteram. Filius vero ipsius vocatus est Benadad, per d in fine: a quo, secundum Hieronymum, posteriores reges Syriæ appellati sunt Benadad, quemadmodum reges Ægypti a primo Pharaone dicti sunt Pharaones, et Cæsares a Cæsare. Sed hoc intelligendum est de generali nomine. Habuerunt enim specialia nomina successores prædicti Benadad et Pharaonis ac Cæsaris. Unde quarto Regum legitur Josias occurrisse Pharaoni Nechao.
paras.en: Next the punishment of the Syrians is added. [[1:4|And I will send a fire|Et mittam ignem]], that is, a heavy punishment, an irrevocable wrath, or captivity, [[1:4|into the house of Azael|in domum Hazael]], that is, upon his offspring; [[1:4|and it shall devour the houses of Benadad|et devorabit domos Benadad]], that is, the descendants, or also the dwellings, of the son of Azael, who was called Benadad. Now the Gloss says that Azael's father was called Benadab, having *b* as its last letter [the Latin says only "having the last letter"; *b* is plainly meant], while his son was called Benadad, with *d* at the end: after whom, according to Jerome, the later kings of Syria were called Benadad, as the kings of Egypt were called Pharaos after the first Pharao, and the Cæsars after Cæsar. But this is to be understood of the general name; for the successors of the said Benadad, and of Pharao and of Cæsar, had particular names. Hence we read in the fourth book of Kings that Josias went to meet Pharao Nechao[[4 Kings 23:29||]].

paras.t: Et conteram vectem Damasci, id est, per manum regis Assyriorum, destruam portas et clausuras, omnemque fortitudinem Damasci ac Syriæ; et disperdam habitatores de campo idoli, id est de Damasco in plano sita, idolisque repleta; et tenentem sceptrum, id est, regem Damasci disperdam, de domo voluptatis et luxuriæ, id est de palatio suo, seu oppido Damasceno, loco deliciosissimo, in quo et ipse et alii vitiis carnis servierunt; et transferetur populus Syriæ Cyrenen, id est, captivus ducetur in Cyrenen, quæ est in ultimis finibus Ægypti, dicit Dominus.
paras.en: [[1:5|And I will break the bar of Damascus|Et conteram vectem Damasci]], that is, by the hand of the king of the Assyrians I will destroy the gates and the bolts and all the strength of Damascus and of Syria; [[1:5|and I will cut off the inhabitants from the plain of the idol|et disperdam habitatores de campo idoli]], that is, from Damascus, which lies on a plain and is full of idols; [[1:5|and him that holdeth the sceptre|et tenentem sceptrum]], that is, I will cut off the king of Damascus, [[1:5|from the house of pleasure|de domo voluptatis]] and of luxury, that is, from his palace, or from the town of Damascus, a most delightful place, in which both he and others were slaves to the vices of the flesh; [[1:5|and the people of Syria shall be carried away to Cyrene|et transferetur populus Syriæ Cyrenen]], that is, they shall be led captive into Cyrene, which is in the furthest borders of Egypt, [[1:5|saith the Lord|dicit Dominus]].

paras.t: Hoc totum impletum est tempore Achaz, ad cujus instantiam Salmanasar rex Assyriorum venit atque vastavit Damascum, et Rasin regem ejus occidit, populum quoque ipsius transtulit Cyrenen, prout quarto Regum recitatur. Unde et in Isaia habetur: Auferetur fortitudo Damasci coram rege Assyriorum.
paras.en: All this was fulfilled in the time of Achaz, at whose instance Salmanasar [the margin corrects this to Theglathphalasar, as in 4 Kings 16:7] king of the Assyrians came and laid Damascus waste, and slew Rasin its king, and carried its people away to Cyrene, as is related in the fourth book of Kings[[4 Kings 16:9||]]. Hence it is said in Isaias too: [[Is 8:4|the strength of Damascus|fortitudo Damasci]] shall be taken away [[Is 8:4|before the king of the Assyrians|coram rege Assyriorum]].

paras.t: Per Moysen demum et Jeremiam Dominus perhibet, se visitaturum peccata patrum in tertiam et quartam generationem. Quod Hieronymus ita hoc loco interpretatur: quod Deus magnitudine suæ clementiæ præstolatur pœnitentiam pereuntium, et quod in prima generatione non vindicat, differt usque ad tertiam et quartam progeniem.
paras.en: Lastly, through Moses and Jeremias the Lord declares that he will visit the sins of the fathers [[Ex 20:5|unto the third and fourth generation|in tertiam et quartam generationem]] [so Moses in Ex 20:5 and Deut 5:9; Jeremias (32:18) speaks of returning the iniquity of the fathers upon their children, without the third and fourth generation]. Jerome interprets this here as follows: that God in the greatness of his clemency waits for the penance of those who are perishing, and what he does not avenge in the first generation, he puts off to the third and fourth.

paras.t: Consequenter subduntur debitæ punitiones Philistinorum, propter injurias populo Israel ab illis illatas. Hæc dicit Dominus: Super tribus sceleribus Gazæ, quæ fuit una de quinque regalibus civitatibus Philistinorum, et super quatuor non convertam eum. Exponenda sunt verba hæc sicut jam exposita sunt verba paulo ante inducta. Est enim sensus: Si habitatores Gazæ semel vel bis præcise persecuti fuissent filios Israel, forsitan parcerem; nunc vero quoniam tertio et quarto hoc fecerunt, non convertam eos ad me. Eo quod transtulerint captivitatem perfectam, id est, partem populi Judæorum ac Israel quam ceperunt, vendiderunt, ut concluderent, id est, claudi ac detineri eam facerent in Idumæa, cujus habitatores fuerunt populo Hebræorum frequenter valde molesti. Dum enim Assyrii vastarent decem tribus, et Chaldæi duas, Philistæi captivaverunt de Israel et de Juda quos poterant, eosque Idumæis vendebant.
paras.en: Next are added the punishments due to the Philistines for the injuries they did to the people of Israel. [[1:6|Thus saith the Lord: For three crimes of Gaza|Hæc dicit Dominus: Super tribus sceleribus Gazæ]], which was one of the five royal cities of the Philistines, [[1:6|and for four I will not convert it|et super quatuor non convertam eum]]. These words are to be explained as the words brought in a little before have been explained. For the sense is: If the inhabitants of Gaza had persecuted the children of Israel just once or twice, perhaps I would spare; but now, since they have done it a third and a fourth time, I will not convert them to me. [[1:6|because they have carried away a perfect captivity|Eo quod transtulerint captivitatem perfectam]], that is, the part of the people of the Jews and of Israel that they took, they sold, [[1:6|to shut them up|ut concluderent]], that is, to have it shut up and kept [[1:6|in Edom|in Idumæa]], whose inhabitants were very often troublesome to the people of the Hebrews. For while the Assyrians were laying waste the ten tribes, and the Chaldeans the two, the Philistines took captive whom they could of Israel and of Juda, and sold them to the Idumeans.

paras.t: Et mittam ignem in murum Gazæ, et devorabit ædes ejus, id est habitacula Gazæ, quam combusserunt Chaldæi. Assyrii quoque ignem tribulationis et persecutionis intulerunt Gazæ, et urbibus quæ subduntur.
paras.en: [[1:7|And I will send a fire on the wall of Gaza, and it shall devour the houses thereof|Et mittam ignem in murum Gazæ, et devorabit ædes ejus]], that is, the dwellings of Gaza, which the Chaldeans burned. The Assyrians too brought the fire of tribulation and persecution upon Gaza and upon the cities named next.

paras.t: Et disperdam habitatorem de Azoto: quæ fuit urbs alia principalis sive metropolis in Philistæa; et tenentem sceptrum, id est, regem Palæstinorum seu regiam potestatem disperdam, de Ascalone, id est alia urbe metropoli Palæstinæ seu terræ Philistinorum. Et forte sedes regni fuit interdum in Ascalone, quæ secundum Glossam antiquitus vocabatur Philistiim. Unde tota regio post appellata est Philistæa, et habitatores ejus Philistiim. Et convertam manum meam, id est potentiam, super Accaron urbem Philistinorum metropolim, dando eam in manus Chaldæorum vel Assyriorum; et peribunt reliquiæ Philistinorum, dicit Dominus Deus, id est ceteræ urbes et vici ac incolæ. Totum enim regnum illud dejecerunt Chaldæi, quemadmodum Isaias, Jeremias et Ezechiel prædixerunt. Quinque autem principales civitates Philistiim sunt, Gaza, Azotus, Ascalon et Accaron, quæ modo expressæ sunt, et Geth quæ hic non explicatur.
paras.en: [[1:8|And I will cut off the inhabitant from Azotus|Et disperdam habitatorem de Azoto]], which was another chief city or capital in Philistia; [[1:8|and him that holdeth the sceptre|et tenentem sceptrum]], that is, I will cut off the king of the Palestinians, or the royal power, [[1:8|from Ascalon|de Ascalone]], that is, from another capital city of Palestine, or of the land of the Philistines. And perhaps the seat of the kingdom was at times in Ascalon, which according to the Gloss was anciently called Philistiim; whence the whole region was afterwards called Philistia, and its inhabitants Philistiim. [[1:8|and I will turn my hand|Et convertam manum meam]], that is, my power, [[1:8|against Accaron|super Accaron]], a capital city of the Philistines, by giving it into the hands of the Chaldeans or the Assyrians; [[1:8|and the rest of the Philistines shall perish, saith the Lord God|et peribunt reliquiæ Philistinorum, dicit Dominus Deus]], that is, the other cities and villages and their inhabitants. For the Chaldeans overthrew that whole kingdom, as Isaias[[Is 11:14||]], Jeremias[[Jer 47:4||]] and Ezechiel[[Ezech 25:16||]] foretold. Now the five chief cities of the Philistiim are Gaza, Azotus, Ascalon and Accaron, which have just been named, and Geth, which is not mentioned here[[1 Kings 6:17||]].

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus: Super tribus sceleribus Tyri, et super quatuor non convertam eum. Exponenda sunt hæc ut supra de Damasco, ut sit sensus: Quoniam Tyrii molesti fuerunt filiis Israel, et persecuti sunt eos tertia vice et quarta, ideo destruentur. Eo quod concluserint captivitatem perfectam, id est, filios Israel a se captos et plene vastatos vendiderunt, et claudi ac detineri fecerunt, in Idumæa, quoniam Idumæis venundabant eos; et non sint recordati Tyrii tam crudeliter agentes, fœderis fratrum, id est pacti fraternitatis et amicitiæ, quod olim fuit inter Hiram regem Tyri, et David ac Salomonem: inter quos jugis pax fuit et amicitia magna, quemadmodum secundo ac tertio Regum plenius scribitur. Porro, homines in Scripturis dicuntur fratres quatuor modis: natura, ut Cain et Abel; cognatione, ut Joab et Amasa; gente, ut omnes Judæi fratres vocantur; amicitia, ut Hiram et Salomon. Unde quum viginti oppida, quæ contulit Salomon Hiram, ipsi Hiram non placuissent: Hæccine, inquit, sunt civitates quas dedisti mihi, frater? Erant enim graminibus plenæ, ut Glossa hic refert.
paras.en: [[1:9|Thus saith the Lord: For three crimes of Tyre, and for four I will not convert it|Hæc dicit Dominus: Super tribus sceleribus Tyri, et super quatuor non convertam eum]]. These words are to be explained as above of Damascus, so that the sense is: Since the Tyrians were troublesome to the children of Israel, and persecuted them a third time and a fourth, therefore they shall be destroyed. [[1:9|because they have shut up an entire captivity|Eo quod concluserint captivitatem perfectam]], that is, they sold the children of Israel whom they had taken and utterly despoiled, and had them shut up and kept [[1:9|in Edom|in Idumæa]], since they sold them to the Idumeans; [[1:9|and have not remembered|et non sint recordati]], the Tyrians, acting so cruelly, [[1:9|the covenant of brethren|fœderis fratrum]], that is, the pact of brotherhood and friendship that was once between Hiram king of Tyre and David and Solomon[[2 Kings 5:11||]][[3 Kings 5:1||]][[3 Kings 5:12||]], between whom there was lasting peace and great friendship, as is written more fully in the second and third books of Kings. Now men are called brothers in the Scriptures in four ways: by nature, as Cain and Abel[[Gen 4:2||]]; by kinship, as Joab and Amasa[[2 Kings 20:9||]]; by nation, as all the Jews are called brothers; by friendship, as Hiram and Solomon. Hence when the twenty towns which Solomon gave to Hiram did not please Hiram, [[3 Kings 9:13|Are these the cities|Hæccine]], he said, [[3 Kings 9:13|which thou hast given me, brother?|sunt civitates quas dedisti mihi, frater?]] For they were overgrown with grass, as the Gloss relates here.

paras.t: Et mittam ignem in murum Tyri, et devorabit ædes ejus. Hoc impletum fuit, quando Nabuchodonosor Tyrum destruxit. Pauca tamen invenit in ea, quoniam negotiatores civesque Tyri per naves fugerunt versus Carthaginem. Propter quod Dominus ait ad Ezechielem: Fili hominis, rex Babylonis servire fecit exercitum suum servitute magna adversus Tyrum, et merces non est reddita ei. Isaias quoque et Jeremias de Tyri destructione vaticinati sunt plurima.
paras.en: [[1:10|And I will send a fire upon the wall of Tyre, and it shall devour the houses thereof|Et mittam ignem in murum Tyri, et devorabit ædes ejus]]. This was fulfilled when Nabuchodonosor destroyed Tyre. Yet he found little in it, because the merchants and citizens of Tyre fled by ship towards Carthage. For which reason the Lord says to Ezechiel: [[Ezech 29:18|Son of man, Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon hath made his army to undergo hard service against Tyre|Fili hominis, rex Babylonis servire fecit exercitum suum servitute magna adversus Tyrum]], [[Ezech 29:18|and there hath been no reward given him|et merces non est reddita ei]]. Isaias[[Is 23:1||]] and Jeremias[[Jer 27:1||]][[Jer 47:4||]] also prophesied a great deal about the destruction of Tyre.

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus Deus: Super tribus sceleribus Edom, id est Idumæorum, qui nati sunt de Esau: qui aliis nominibus dictus est Edom, id est rufus vel sanguineus; et Seir, id est pilosus seu hispidus; et super quatuor non convertam eum: id est, quoniam tertio et quarto persecuti sunt populum meum Israel, non eis ignoscam, sed graviter puniam. Eo quod persecutus sit in gladio fratrem suum: id est, quemadmodum Esau persecutus est Jacob, ita ut fugeret Jacob in Mesopotamiam, sic populus Idumæorum persecutus est in gladio populum Judæorum de Jacob exortum; et violaverit misericordiam ejus, id est, pietatem, ad quam naturali jure tenebatur, non exhibuit fratri suo præfato. Quum enim duo populi isti ex duobus fratribus, scilicet Esau et Jacob, processerint, debuerunt sibi invicem omnem misericordiam in omnibus exhibere; sed populus Idumæorum ita non egit. Imo nec voluit filiis Israel ascendentibus ex Ægypto iter præbere per terram suam, sed dixit: Non transibis per me, alioqui armatus occurram tibi. Statimque cum infinita multitudine exierunt rex Edom et populus ejus. Propter quod declinavit Israel ab eo, quemadmodum in Numerorum libro legitur. Et tenuerit ultra furorem suum, id est, implacabili inveterataque ira exarsit in populum Israel; et indignationem suam contra Israel servaverit usque in finem, id est usque ad captivitatem Judæorum a Chaldæis, seu decem tribuum ab Assyriis, hoc est, quamdiu filii Israel manserunt in terra promissionis.
paras.en: [[1:11|Thus saith the Lord: For three crimes of Edom|Hæc dicit Dominus Deus: Super tribus sceleribus Edom]], that is, of the Idumeans, who were born of Esau, who by other names was called Edom, that is, red or ruddy[[Gen 25:30||]], and Seir, that is, hairy or rough[[Gen 25:25||]]; [[1:11|and for four I will not convert him|et super quatuor non convertam eum]]: that is, since they have persecuted my people Israel a third and a fourth time, I will not forgive them, but will punish them heavily. [[1:11|because he hath pursued his brother with the sword|Eo quod persecutus sit in gladio fratrem suum]]: that is, as Esau persecuted Jacob, so that Jacob fled into Mesopotamia[[Gen 27:41||]][[Gen 28:5||]], so the people of the Idumeans persecuted with the sword the people of the Jews sprung from Jacob; and hath violated his mercy [*et violaverit misericordiam ejus*: these words of the Vulgate are missing from the Douay-Rheims text used here], that is, he did not show his aforesaid brother the kindness to which he was bound by natural law. For since these two peoples came from two brothers, namely Esau and Jacob[[Gen 25:23||]], they ought to have shown each other all mercy in all things; but the people of the Idumeans did not do so. Indeed, they would not even give the children of Israel, as they came up out of Egypt, a way through their land, but said: [[Num 20:18|Thou shalt not pass by me: if thou dost I will come out armed against thee|Non transibis per me, alioqui armatus occurram tibi]]. And at once the king of Edom and his people came out with an infinite multitude[[Num 20:20||]]; for which reason Israel turned away from him[[Num 20:21||]], as we read in the book of Numbers. [[1:11|and hath carried on his fury|Et tenuerit ultra furorem suum]], that is, he burned with implacable and inveterate anger against the people of Israel; [[1:11|and hath kept his wrath|et indignationem suam]] against Israel [[1:11|to the end|servaverit usque in finem]], that is, until the captivity of the Jews by the Chaldeans, or of the ten tribes by the Assyrians; that is, as long as the children of Israel remained in the land of promise.

paras.t: Mittam ignem in Theman, et devorabit ædes Bosræ. Quidam per Theman intelligunt metropolim Idumææ, et per Bosram aliam Idumææ civitatem. Hieronymus vero affirmat, quod Theman sit hic nomen regionis Idumæorum, et similiter Bosra, ita quod utrumque eamdem significat terram.
paras.en: [[1:12|I will send a fire into Theman: and it shall devour the houses of Bosra|Mittam ignem in Theman, et devorabit ædes Bosræ]]. Some understand by Theman the capital of Idumea, and by Bosra another city of Idumea. But Jerome affirms that Theman is here the name of the region of the Idumeans, and likewise Bosra, so that both signify the same land.

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus: Super tribus sceleribus filiorum Ammon, id est Ammonitarum descendentium de semine Lot ex filia sua juniori, et super quatuor, id est propter eorum impietatem toties repetitam, et in filios Israel factam, non convertam eum, id est populum Ammonitarum a suis peccatis et debitis pœnis; eo quod dissecuerit prægnantes Galaad, id est mulieres prægnantes Jabes Galaad, ne parerent pueros possessuros terram Galaad, quam Ammonitæ laborabant acquirere. Ideo subditur: ad dilatandum terminum suum, id est terram seu fines patriæ suæ. Optabant enim totam terram Galaad suo addere atque subjicere regno. Hoc fuit tempore Saul, quando Naas rex filiorum Ammon impugnavit Galaad, et prægnantes ejus divisit. Quumque (ut primo Regum recolitur) habitatores Jabes Galaad mandassent regi Ammon, Habe nos confœderatos; respondit, In hoc habebo vos fœderatos, ut eruam omnium vestrum oculos dexteros. Quoniam ergo Ammonitæ ab illo tempore et ante, usque ad tempus Amos prophetæ, manserunt in sua crudelitate et injuriatione contra Israelitas, tradidit eos Dominus in manus Chaldæorum, sicut subjungitur.
paras.en: [[1:13|Thus saith the Lord: For three crimes of the children of Ammon|Hæc dicit Dominus: Super tribus sceleribus filiorum Ammon]], that is, of the Ammonites, descended from the seed of Lot by his younger daughter[[Gen 19:38||]], [[1:13|and for four|et super quatuor]], that is, for their impiety so often repeated and done against the children of Israel, [[1:13|I will not convert him|non convertam eum]], that is, the people of the Ammonites, from their sins and from the punishments they deserve; [[1:13|because he hath ripped up the women with child of Galaad|eo quod dissecuerit prægnantes Galaad]], that is, the women with child of Jabes Galaad, so that they should not bear sons who would possess the land of Galaad, which the Ammonites were striving to acquire. Therefore it is added: [[1:13|to enlarge his border|ad dilatandum terminum suum]], that is, the land or the bounds of their country. For they wished to add the whole land of Galaad to their kingdom and subject it to it. This was in the time of Saul, when Naas king of the children of Ammon attacked Galaad and ripped up its women with child. And when (as is recalled in the first book of Kings) the inhabitants of Jabes Galaad sent word to the king of Ammon, [[1 Kings 11:1|Make a covenant with us|Habe nos confœderatos]], he answered, [[1 Kings 11:2|On this condition will I make a covenant with you, that I may pluck out all your right eyes|In hoc habebo vos fœderatos, ut eruam omnium vestrum oculos dexteros]]. Since therefore the Ammonites, from that time and before it until the time of the prophet Amos, persisted in their cruelty and wrongdoing against the Israelites, the Lord delivered them into the hands of the Chaldeans, as is added next.

paras.t: Et succendam ignem in muro Rabba metropolis Ammonitarum, quæ in Deuteronomio et in secundo Regum vocatur Rabbath. Ignis autem intelligitur demolitio seu gravis punitio civitatis et habitatorum ipsius. Et devorabit ædes ejus, id est, habitacula destruet, in ululatu, id est clamore exercitus destruentis hanc urbem, vel in lamentatione et sono confuso Ammonitarum cadentium gladio Chaldæorum, in die belli Chaldæorum contra Ammonitas, et in turbine, id est abundanti calamitate Ammonitarum, quæ fuit similis tempestati, in die commotionis, qua ab hostibus moti sunt, territi, interfecti, sive translati.
paras.en: [[1:14|And I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabba|Et succendam ignem in muro Rabba]], the capital of the Ammonites, which in Deuteronomy and in the second book of Kings is called Rabbath[[Deut 3:11||]][[2 Kings 12:26||]]. By the fire is understood the demolition or heavy punishment of the city and of its inhabitants. [[1:14|and it shall devour the houses thereof|Et devorabit ædes ejus]], that is, it shall destroy the dwellings, [[1:14|with shouting|in ululatu]], that is, with the clamour of the army destroying this city, or with the lamentation and confused noise of the Ammonites falling by the sword of the Chaldeans, [[1:14|in the day of battle|in die belli]] of the Chaldeans against the Ammonites, [[1:14|and with a whirlwind|et in turbine]], that is, with the overflowing calamity of the Ammonites, which was like a tempest, [[1:14|in the day of trouble|in die commotionis]], on which they were moved [*moti*, playing on *commotio*, "commotion"] by the enemy, terrified, slain or carried away.

paras.t: Et ibit Melchom, id est rex Ammonitarum, qui per idolum quod coluit, nomine Melchom, designatur, in captivitatem, quia rex Chaldæorum cepit eum, ipse et principes ejus, id est sacerdotes seu alii potentes ac nobiles, simul, id est, pariter cum rege suo captivi ducentur, dicit Dominus. De hac re in aliis Prophetis plenius legitur.
paras.en: [[1:15|And Melchom shall go|Et ibit Melchom]], that is, the king of the Ammonites, who is signified by the idol he worshipped, named Melchom, [[1:15|into captivity|in captivitatem]], for the king of the Chaldeans took him captive, [[1:15|both he, and his princes|ipse et principes ejus]], that is, the priests or other mighty and noble men, [[1:15|together|simul]], that is, they shall be led captive along with their king, [[1:15|saith the Lord|dicit Dominus]]. Of this more is read in the other Prophets.

1.title: Expositio moralis ejusdem primi capituli.
1.title_en: Moral exposition of the same first chapter.

paras.t: Verba Amos, qui fuit in pastoralibus Thecue. Amos interpretatur onustus, sive avulsus; Thecue vero, clangens tuba. Qui ergo onustus est, id est observantiis divinorum præceptorum subjectus, portans pondus diei et æstus, qui mortificatur pro Deo tota die, hic audit verba secreta a Deo, ita ut dicat cum Isaia: Dominus Deus aperuit mihi aurem; ego autem non contradico. Omnis enim sanctus instinctus, omnis inspiratio sancta, omnis consideratio bona, est interna quædam Dei locutio, quia non sumus sufficientes cogitare aliquid ex nobis, quasi ex nobis. Talis quoque, conversatur et est in pastoralibus Thecue, id est in spiritualibus escis, in corporali opulentia Dei omnipotentis, per Scripturas et sanctos prædicatores atque doctores catholicos, quasi per tubam clangentis et populum erudientis. Potestque dicere: Dominus regit me, et nihil mihi deerit, in loco pascuæ ibi me collocavit; super aquam refectionis educavit me. Vel est in pastoralibus, id est locis seu congregationibus Ecclesiæ, quæ per modum tubæ vocem suam exaltat, Deinde verba enuntiat: in quibus utique locis fideles verbis et exemplis bonorum prælatorum aluntur, sacramentalibus quoque gratiis reficiuntur.
paras.en: [[1:1|The words of Amos, who was among the herdsmen of Thecua|Verba Amos, qui fuit in pastoralibus Thecue]] [Denis's text reads *in pastoralibus*, "among the pastures", where the Douay-Rheims has "among the herdsmen"; his gloss takes it of pastures]. *Amos* is interpreted "burdened", or "torn away"; *Thecue*, "sounding the trumpet". He, then, who is burdened, that is, subject to the observances of the divine commandments, who has [[Matt 20:12|borne the burden of the day and the heats|portans pondus diei et æstus]], who is put to death for God all the day long[[Ps 43:22||]], hears secret words from God, so that he may say with Isaias: [[Is 50:5|The Lord God hath opened my ear, and I do not resist|Dominus Deus aperuit mihi aurem; ego autem non contradico]]. For every holy impulse, every holy inspiration, every good thought is a kind of inward speaking of God, because we are not [[2 Cor 3:5|sufficient to think any thing of ourselves, as of ourselves|sufficientes cogitare aliquid ex nobis, quasi ex nobis]]. Such a one also dwells and is among the pastures of Thecue, that is, among spiritual foods, in the bodily abundance [so the print, *corporali*; the sense would rather want "plentiful"] of almighty God, who sounds as with a trumpet and teaches the people through the Scriptures and the holy preachers and catholic doctors. And he can say: [[Ps 22:1|The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing|Dominus regit me, et nihil mihi deerit]], [[Ps 22:2|He hath set me in a place of pasture. He hath brought me up, on the water of refreshment|in loco pascuæ ibi me collocavit; super aquam refectionis educavit me]]. Or he is among the pastures, that is, in the places or congregations of the Church, which lifts up her voice like a trumpet, then utters words [so the print, *Deinde*; perhaps to be read *Dei*, "utters the words of God"]: in which places, indeed, the faithful are fed by the words and examples of good prelates, and refreshed also by sacramental graces.

paras.t: Dominus de Sion rugiet: id est, de Ecclesia per ora prædicantium terribiles comminationes effundet, dicendo illud in Luca: Væ vobis qui nunc ridetis; væ vobis divitibus; væ vobis qui saturati estis. Et de Jerusalem, id est de hac ipsa Ecclesia, dabit vocem suam, id est verba dulcis consolationis ac magnæ promissionis, dicendo: Vado parare vobis locum; et, Ubi ego sum, illic et minister meus erit; et, Qui diligit me, diligetur a Patre meo, et ego diligam eum, et ad eum veniemus, et mansionem apud eum faciemus. Hæc facit Deus quotidie. Sion interpretatur speculatio; Jerusalem autem, visio pacis. Ecclesia ergo contemplando divina dicitur Sion, et pacem habendo intusque cernendo, appellatur Jerusalem.
paras.en: [[1:2|The Lord will roar from Sion|Dominus de Sion rugiet]]: that is, from the Church, through the mouths of preachers, he will pour out terrible threats, saying that word in Luke: [[Luke 6:25|Woe to you that now laugh|Væ vobis qui nunc ridetis]]; [[Luke 6:24|woe to you that are rich|væ vobis divitibus]]; [[Luke 6:25|Woe to you that are filled|væ vobis qui saturati estis]]. And [[1:2|from Jerusalem|de Jerusalem]], that is, from this same Church, he will [[1:2|utter his voice|dabit vocem suam]], that is, words of sweet consolation and of great promise, saying: [[John 14:2|I go to prepare a place for you|Vado parare vobis locum]]; and, [[John 12:26|where I am, there also shall my minister be|Ubi ego sum, illic et minister meus erit]]; and, [[John 14:21|he that loveth me shall be loved of my Father: and I will love him|Qui diligit me, diligetur a Patre meo, et ego diligam eum]], [[John 14:23|and we will come to him and will make our abode with him|et ad eum veniemus, et mansionem apud eum faciemus]]. This God does daily. *Sion* is interpreted "watching" [*speculatio*, looking out as from a watchtower]; *Jerusalem*, "vision of peace". The Church, then, in contemplating divine things is called Sion, and in having peace and beholding inwardly is called Jerusalem.

paras.t: Et luxerunt speciosa pastorum, id est decor et gloria eorum qui solo nomine sunt pastores (de quibus in Isaia habetur: Ipsi pastores ignoraverunt intelligentiam; canes muti desolati sunt et evanuerunt): quia dum Christus per sanctos suos verosque pastores in Ecclesia loquitur, inutiles pastores confunduntur, tristantur, et inanes esse noscuntur. Et exsiccatus est vertex Carmeli, id est, mundana sapientia per inanem eloquentiam decorata, sterilis facta est, quemadmodum dicit Apostolus: Stultam fecit Deus sapientiam hujus mundi.
paras.en: [[1:2|and the beautiful places of the shepherds have mourned|Et luxerunt speciosa pastorum]], that is, the comeliness and glory of those who are shepherds in name only (of whom it is said in Isaias: [[Is 56:11|the shepherds themselves knew no understanding|Ipsi pastores ignoraverunt intelligentiam]]; [[Is 56:10|dumb dogs|canes muti]] are become desolate and have vanished away [these last words are not in Isaias]): because while Christ speaks in the Church through his saints and true shepherds, the useless shepherds are confounded, are saddened, and are known to be empty. [[1:2|and the top of Carmel is withered|Et exsiccatus est vertex Carmeli]], that is, worldly wisdom, adorned with empty eloquence, has become barren, as the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 1:20|God made foolish the wisdom of this world?|Stultam fecit Deus sapientiam hujus mundi]]

paras.t: Super tribus sceleribus Damasci, et super quatuor non convertam eum. Primum peccatum, est motus passionum in appetitu inferiori, vel cogitatio mala; secundum, est consensus rationis; tertium, exsecutio operis. Quæ designantur per tres mortuos a Christo resuscitatos: primum, per filiam Jairi archisynagogi, quam suscitavit in domo; secundum, per filium viduæ extra civitatem, quia consensus rationis est extra et supra sensualitatem; tertium, per Lazarum clausum, quoniam opus malum tanquam lapis gravat et opprimit prævaricantem. Quartum peccatum est, non pœnitere de malo. Super tribus autem sceleribus Deus frequenter convertit, sed impœnitentem æternaliter damnat. Talis namque quum in profundum peccatorum venerit, contemnit, nec levat oculos suos, ut adspiciat cœlum; sed claudit super eum puteus os suum. Unde et Christus non legitur quartum mortuum suscitasse, quia per corporalem suscitationem, spiritualis figurabatur.
paras.en: [[1:3|For three crimes of Damascus, and for four I will not convert it|Super tribus sceleribus Damasci, et super quatuor non convertam eum]]. The first sin is the motion of the passions in the lower appetite, or an evil thought; the second is the consent of the reason; the third, the carrying out of the deed. These are signified by the three dead raised by Christ: the first by the daughter of Jairus, the ruler of the synagogue, whom he raised in the house[[Mark 5:22||]]; the second by the widow's son, outside the city[[Luke 7:11||]], because the consent of the reason is outside and above the sensuality [that is, the sense appetite, the lower part of the soul]; the third by Lazarus shut in the tomb[[John 11:1||]], because the evil deed weighs down and crushes the transgressor like a stone. The fourth sin is not to repent of the evil. Now for three crimes God often converts [that is, turns back from punishing], but the impenitent he condemns eternally. For such a one, [[Prov 18:3|when he is come into the depths of sins, contemneth|quum in profundum peccatorum venerit, contemnit]], and does not lift up his eyes to look upon heaven; but [[Ps 68:16|the pit shut her mouth|claudit super eum puteus os suum]] upon him [Denis has *claudit*, "shuts", where the Psalm has *urgeat*]. Hence too Christ is not read to have raised a fourth dead man, because by the bodily raising the spiritual one was figured.

paras.t: Damascus præterea interpretatur, bibens sanguinem. Sicque significat subversores aliorum, qui vitam spiritualem eorum quos fallunt, consumunt et ebibunt; qui prægnantes, id est animas in bonis fecundas, triturant in plaustris ferreis, id est, acutis versutiis, minis, seu tribulationibus destruunt, avertendo eas a Deo : propter quod dicuntur prægnantes Galaad, id est transmigrationis, quia recedunt a Deo, transmigrantes in montem vanitatis sicut passer, quæ ante hanc suam seductionem dicere poterant illud Isaiæ : A facie tua, Domine, concepimus et quasi parturivimus. Quæ autem non seducuntur, addere possunt quod ibi adjungitur : Et peperimus spiritum.
paras.en: Moreover *Damascus* is interpreted "drinking blood". And so it signifies those who overthrow others, who consume and drink up the spiritual life of those whom they deceive; who thresh the women with child, that is, souls fruitful in good things, [[1:3|with iron wains|in plaustris ferreis]], that is, destroy them by sharp cunning, threats or tribulations, turning them away from God [the women with child stand in this verse in the Septuagint; in the Vulgate they appear in v. 13]: for which reason they are called the women with child of [[1:3|Galaad|Galaad]], that is, of migration, because they depart from God, migrating into the mountain of vanity like a sparrow[[Ps 10:2||]]; they who before this their seduction could say that of Isaias: [[Is 26:17|in thy presence, O Lord|A facie tua, Domine]], [[Is 26:18|We have conceived, and been as it were in labour|concepimus et quasi parturivimus]]. But those who are not seduced can add what is joined to it there: [[Is 26:18|and have brought forth wind|Et peperimus spiritum]] [*spiritum* is "spirit" as well as "wind"; Denis takes it in the good sense].

paras.t: Mittit ergo Dominus ignem suæ vindictæ, in domum Hazael, id est eorum qui alios ita subvertunt; qui devorat domos Benadad, id est congregationem consentientium, sequentium, vel cooperantium malo.
paras.en: The Lord therefore sends the fire of his vengeance [[1:4|into the house of Azael|in domum Hazael]], that is, of those who thus overthrow others; which devours [[1:4|the houses of Benadad|domos Benadad]], that is, the congregation of those who consent to the evil, follow it, or work with it.

paras.t: Et conteram vectem Damasci, id est fortitudinem præfatorum animas manducantium, seu sanguinem aliorum bibentium. Dicit autem Haymo, quod servus Abrahæ Damascus Eliezer, condidit urbem Damascum in campo ubi occisus est Abel. Et disperdam habitatores de campo idoli, id est homines terrenos, in campo idoli, id est in latitudine mundi, in quo idola vanitatis ac falsitatis colunt : dum alii in suis sophismatibus jugiter occupantur et gloriantur, aliorum deus venter est, aliorum, aurum aut venus; alii cum stultis vanisque cogitationibus quasi cum idolis ludunt, non advertentes illud Joannis : Custodite vos a simulacris; et illud Michæe, Væ vobis qui cogitatis inutile.
paras.en: [[1:5|And I will break the bar of Damascus|Et conteram vectem Damasci]], that is, the strength of the aforesaid, who devour souls, or drink the blood of others. Now Haymo says that Abraham's servant, Damascus Eliezer, founded the city of Damascus in the field where Abel was slain[[Gen 4:8||]]. [[1:5|and I will cut off the inhabitants from the plain of the idol|Et disperdam habitatores de campo idoli]], that is, earthly men, in the plain of the idol, that is, in the breadth of the world, in which they worship idols of vanity and falsehood: while some are ever busied with their sophistries and glory in them; others are those [[Phil 3:19|whose God is their belly|deus venter est]], others those whose god is gold or lust; others play with foolish and vain thoughts as with idols, not heeding that word of John: [[1 John 5:21|keep yourselves from idols|Custodite vos a simulacris]]; and that of Micheas: [[Mich 2:1|Woe to you that devise that which is unprofitable|Væ vobis qui cogitatis inutile]].

paras.t: Insuper, per punitionem Tyri (quæ interpretatur angustia), figuratur eorum damnatio qui non ambulant in latitudine caritatis nec dicere possunt cum Apostolo, Cor nostrum dilatatum est; sed frigore invidientiæ constringuntur, et privato amore sic coarctantur, quod non quærunt nisi quæ sua sunt, non communicantes proximis dona Dei sibi concessa.
paras.en: Further, by the punishment of Tyre (which is interpreted "narrowness") is figured the damnation of those who do not walk in the breadth of charity, nor can say with the Apostle, [[2 Cor 6:11|our heart is enlarged|Cor nostrum dilatatum est]]; but are bound tight by the cold of envy, and so narrowed by private love that they seek nothing but [[Phil 2:21|the things that are their own|quæ sua sunt]], not sharing with their neighbours the gifts of God granted to them.

paras.t: Per punitionem vero Edom (quæ interpretatur rubens vel sanguinea), figuratur damnatio hominum sanguinolentorum, qui in operibus carnis et sanguinis volutantur, rubent et inflammantur : et maxime infidelis Synagoga, quæ fratrem suum, id est primitivam Ecclesiam ex Judaismo conversam, persecuta est usque ad sanguinem. De quibus ait Christus in Isaia : Adspersus est sanguis eorum super vestimenta mea; itemque in Evangelio : Ut veniat super vos omnis sanguis justus qui effusus est super terram, etc. De talibus cantamus in Psalmo : Viri sanguinum et dolosi non dimidiabunt dies suos. Verum ut ait Apostolus, Caro et sanguis regnum Dei non possidebunt.
paras.en: But by the punishment of Edom (which is interpreted "red" or "bloody") is figured the damnation of men of blood, who wallow in the works of flesh and blood, grow red and are inflamed: and above all the unbelieving Synagogue, which persecuted [[1:11|his brother|fratrem suum]], that is, the early Church converted from Judaism, even unto blood. Of these Christ says in Isaias: [[Is 63:3|their blood is sprinkled upon my garments|Adspersus est sanguis eorum super vestimenta mea]]; and likewise in the Gospel: [[Matt 23:35|That upon you may come all the just blood that hath been shed upon the earth|Ut veniat super vos omnis sanguis justus qui effusus est super terram]], etc. Of such we sing in the Psalm: [[Ps 54:24|Bloody and deceitful men shall not live out half their days|Viri sanguinum et dolosi non dimidiabunt dies suos]]. But, as the Apostle says, [[1 Cor 15:50|flesh and blood cannot possess the kingdom of God|Caro et sanguis regnum Dei non possidebunt]].

paras.t: Postremo, per punitionem filiorum Ammon (qui interpretatur populus meus, vel populus mœroris), intelligitur damnatio impiorum Christianorum, qui sunt populus Dei per fidem, non per caritatem et opera, qui sine veste nuptiali venire præsumunt ad militantis Ecclesiæ nuptias. Quos certum est inordinatis mœroribus affici : quoniam contristantur in quibus contristandum non est, utpote propter præsentis vitæ adversa; et non contristantur in quibus tristandum est, scilicet propter sua et aliorum peccata, et cetera animæ nocumenta peccatum consequentia. Et præsertim contristari debemus de hoc, quod Deum sanctum, pium ac liberalissimum, toties inhonoramus, beneficiis ejus ingrati, et coram præsentia majestatis ejus intimorati.
paras.en: Lastly, by the punishment of the children of Ammon (which is interpreted "my people", or "people of sorrow") is understood the damnation of wicked Christians, who are the people of God by faith, not by charity and works, who presume to come without the wedding garment to the wedding of the Church militant. It is certain that these are touched by disordered sorrows: for they are saddened where there is no cause for sadness, as by the adversities of the present life; and are not saddened where there is cause for sadness, namely by their own sins and those of others, and the other harms to the soul that follow upon sin. And above all we ought to be saddened at this, that we so often dishonour God, holy, loving and most generous, ungrateful for his benefits, and without fear before the presence of his majesty.

paras.t: Moralitatem autem hujus capituli per singula verba, propter prolixitatem vitandam, non prosequor, præsertim quum sententia moralitatis hujus sæpe jam posita sit.
paras.en: But I do not follow out the moral sense of this chapter word by word, to avoid prolixity, especially since the substance of this moral sense has often been set down already.
